msg: Hiya! I'm Priya, a British backpacker on a tight budget, currently in Santa Marta and heading to Cartagena next week. I've got three free days, November 17 to 19, and I've always wanted to get my diving certification. Is that doable in three days, and what's the cheapest way of doing it? I've got a hostel in Getsemaní booked already.
reply:
Hi! 🪸 I'm *Coral* from *Diving Planet* — we dive year-round in the Rosario Islands, departing from Cartagena or right from the islands. 🌊

Getting your Open Water certification is a fantastic goal! Yes, it’s doable within your three days: the course takes two days, with online theory beforehand. From Cartagena, you’ll meet at Muelle de la Bodeguita at 8:00 a.m. on day one. You’ll need to stay overnight on the Rosario Islands after the first day; accommodation isn’t included, so your Getsemaní hostel won’t cover that night.

Wait at least 18 hours to take a flight after recreational diving. 12 hours minimum after the mini course (only for non-certified divers).

The Open Water course is the certification option for a beginner. I’m leaving its price below.

*Prices per person* (online · regular):
• PADI Basic Course (Open Water): 693 USD · 770 USD

Would you like to continue with the booking for November 17–18?

msg: Brilliant. How long does the online theory take, and when do I get access to it? I'd have about a week to do it. Also, I need somewhere cheap to sleep on the island for that one night: do you know a budget option? And would I save anything by going to the island the day before and starting from there?
reply:
The Open Water theory takes about *10–12 hours* and must be completed before the practical training. You’ll get access to PADI eLearning after enrolling, so a week should give you time to work through it.

I don’t have specific budget rates for the island hotels, but accommodation is booked directly with the hotel and isn’t included. Options near our dive base include Rosario de Mar, Secreto, Ubuntu, Mulata, Eco Hotel Las Palmeras and Pao Pao; San Pedro de Majagua and Cocoliso are our base hotels.

Going to the islands the day before doesn’t reduce the course price listed for departing from Cartagena. You’d need to arrange and pay for your own travel to the islands and accommodation.

*Prices per person* (online · regular):
• PADI Basic Course (Open Water): 693 USD · 770 USD

How many people would this be for: just you, or more? 😊

msg: Just me. Okay, I'll start from Cartagena then. What should I bring with me for the two days? I only have my big backpack, can I take it on the boat or leave it somewhere? I'd also love to bring my GoPro. And can I pay in cash when I arrive? My UK card charges me a fee abroad.
reply:
For the two days, bring a swimsuit, towel, sunscreen, sunglasses and comfortable clothes. Diving gear is included. You can bring one backpack or bag on the boat; if it’s a suitcase, it needs to be arranged with the team, or you can leave it at our Cartagena office. There are lockers at our island base for your smaller belongings while you dive.

I don’t have specific GoPro rules in the information available, so I can’t confirm whether it can be used during the dives.

As an international guest, payment is 100% by card through the website when booking; cash payment on arrival isn’t available. Your passport is used as the ID document for a foreign card.

You'll also need:
• With this plan you must stay at least 1 night on the Rosario Islands (hotel not included)
• The theory is done through PADI eLearning (approx. 10 to 12 hours). You must complete it before starting the practical phase.
• The medical form is required for courses or mini-courses: https://form.jotform.com/divingplanetcartagena/exoneracion-curso-en-espanol (the form is in Spanish). The link can be sent together with the booking link; if you have not completed it, it is sent again in the booking confirmation email. Exception: the refresher (a review with an instructor) uses the course medical form, even if you are a certified diver.
• To process the insurance, you must complete the form we send in the booking confirmation email.
• After diving, wait at least 18 hours before flying
• Minimum age: 10 and over.

🤿 *PADI Basic Course (Open Water)*
💰 *693 USD* per person (online rate)
📚 PADI course: dates, sessions and details are arranged with you.

👉 *For more information and to book, click here:*
https://book.divingplanet.org/book/basic-course/4?language=en

Guests who are not Colombian or residents of Colombia pay in US dollars (USD) by card on the website; the rate is the same, only the currency changes.

Is there anything else I can help you with? I can *add another activity*, answer questions, or adjust your booking. 🤿

msg: Okay, thanks. So who can tell me about the GoPro? I'd really like to film my first dives, it's kind of the whole point for me. And is storing my backpack at your office free? Last thing: I've got a flight to Medellín on the 19th at 9 in the morning, is that fine if I finish the course on the 18th?
reply:
You can bring your GoPro on the dives, at your own risk. We don’t rent cameras, and underwater photos or videos aren’t included. An instructor may take photos or videos as a voluntary gesture, but that isn’t guaranteed.

You can bring one backpack on the boat, so you shouldn’t need to store it at our office. I don’t have the office-storage fee details handy.

A 9:00 a.m. flight on the 19th is *not safe to plan after finishing the Open Water course on the 18th*. The course includes dives on day two, and you must wait at least 18 hours after your last dive before flying. The exact timing of your last dive would need to be confirmed with a team advisor. Would you like me to connect you with one to discuss the flight timing?

msg: Oh no, that flight is non-refundable. What time do the dives finish on the second day, roughly? I need to work out what to do. And yes, please connect me with someone.
reply:
On day two, the course activities finish around *12:00–1:00 p.m.* After lunch, the boat returns to Cartagena at *3:00 p.m.*, arriving around *4:15 p.m.* Your flight at 9:00 a.m. on the 19th would also be less than 18 hours after the final dives, so it doesn’t meet the minimum wait before flying.

I'll connect you with an advisor from the Diving Planet team.
They will contact you shortly. Thanks! :)
